title: Preventive fallback stabilizer: windowed reopen and load trim hotfix
author: Anika Patel
description:
Motivation: Production incidents showed repeated reopen flapping when a regional circuit briefly recovered; this caused rapid request spill and destabilized downstream nodes. We need a short-term stabilizer that dampens reopen events by applying a windowed reopen allowance and an aggressive short-term load-trim to prevent overshoot while preserving SLOs for high-priority routes.

Summary: Implement a preventive fallback stabilizer that: 1) tracks per-region reopen events in a sliding window and prevents reopen attempts if reopen rate exceeds a threshold; 2) introduces a temporary, rapidly-decaying load-trim that reduces admitted requests for non-critical tenants/routes for the first 30s after a reopen; 3) emits detailed metrics and audit logs for each suppressed reopen and trimmed route to aid post-incident analysis; 4) exposes two knobs in the runtime config (window_size_secs, reopen_rate_threshold_pct) and a feature flag for staged rollout.

What changed (high level): added stabilizer component to runtime/circuit, integrated with the SLO enforcer to coordinate prioritized trimming, added region probe hysteresis to avoid premature reopen signals, surfaced metrics and traces to observability, and added unit + integration tests covering edge cases.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4132)
- [x] Feature flag gated and defaulted off in config
- [x] Unit tests for reopen window logic
- [x] Integration test simulating rapid reopen cycles
- [x] Metrics dashboards updated (temporary)
- [x] Rollout plan included in PR description

Rollout plan: feature flag disabled by default. Canary rollout to a single low-risk region for 24h with increased sampling. If metrics show reduced reopen churn and stable high-priority SLOs, progressively enable for additional regions in 6-hour increments. If regressions appear, flip feature flag off and failover to previous behavior.

Testing: CI runs unit + integration suites. Manual chaos test performed on staging by inducing rapid circuit toggles; observed reduced reopen attempts, and trimmed load prevented downstream saturation. Load-trim decay verified (linear decay from 60% trim at t=0 to 0% at t=30s).

Rollback: revert flag and configuration; code instrumentation includes a short-circuit that restores previous behavior without a restart when feature flag is toggled.

Notes: This is intentionally conservative and focused on behavior stabilization, not permanent policy changes. Follow-up PR will evaluate longer-term heuristics and telemetry-driven automatic thresholds (ENG-4150).

review_comments: Diego Morales: The reopen window default of 60s might be too long for low-latency services. Can we make the window configurable per tier?
Anika Patel: Responded: Good point — added tiered override support in the config (per-priority overrides) and updated tests to exercise the overrides.
Jin Park: Suggest adding a metric that records when the load-trim prevented an Admit to correlate with downstream saturation incidents.
Anika Patel: Responded: Added trimmed_route_count and included trace ids in the audit log so operators can reconstruct the decision path.
Lena Fischer: Integration test looks good but flaky on first run; observed a race in the probe hysteresis timer. Please add a deterministic clock in tests.
Anika Patel: Responded: Switched the integration test to use a fake clock and reran — flake resolved. CI rerun confirmed stability.
Diego Morales: Approving after the tiered config change and adding a short note in the runbook about destructive testing limits.
Jin Park: Approved — good safeguards and observability.
release_notes:
- Hotfix: add a preventive fallback stabilizer to reduce reopen flapping and prevent downstream saturation
- New runtime knobs: window_size_secs, reopen_rate_threshold_pct, per-priority overrides
- New metrics: reopen_suppressed_count, trimmed_route_count
- Feature is feature-flagged and disabled by default; follow the canary checklist in docs/operational/reopen-stabilizer.md
